subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Simplify ³⁴C₅ + Σ ⁽³⁸⁻ʳ⁾C₄, the sum taken over r = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.

mark_split.label: Write out the five terms of the sum
Repeat the identity until one term is left

recall_prompt: Say how you would simplify this sum of combinations — what you write out first, which identity you use, and how it collapses.
insider_note: The chain must be written line by line — ³⁵C₅, ³⁶C₅, ³⁷C₅, ³⁸C₅, then ³⁹C₅ — because two of the four marks are those lines, and a jump straight from the sum to ³⁹C₅ skips them. Start at the 34 pair, the only pair with a C₅ partner.

steps.label: Write out the sum
steps.margin_note: First mark. Put r = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 into ⁽³⁸⁻ʳ⁾C₄ and list the five terms. Then place ³⁴C₅ next to ³⁴C₄ — the two with the smallest top number go together.

recall.must_convey: That the sigma is expanded into its five terms ³⁸C₄ down to ³⁴C₄ and written next to ³⁴C₅.
accept: put r equal to zero to four and write the five terms thirty eight C four down to thirty four C four
expand the sigma into thirty eight C four plus thirty seven C four and so on to thirty four C four
write out all five terms of the sum and put thirty four C five with them
sigma ni expand chesi five terms rayali, thirty four C five pakkana thirty four C four pettali
list the terms of the sum from r equals zero to four

steps.why: Nothing can be simplified while the terms are hidden inside a sigma. Written out, the terms ³⁴C₄ and ³⁴C₅ sit side by side and the identity can start.
common_mistakes: Writing four terms instead of five — r = 0 gives ³⁸C₄ and r = 4 gives ³⁴C₄, both included.
Leaving ³⁴C₅ at the far end instead of next to ³⁴C₄.

steps.label: Apply the identity once
steps.margin_note: Second mark. State ⁿCᵣ₋₁ + ⁿCᵣ = ⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾Cᵣ and use it on the pair with top number 34: ³⁴C₄ + ³⁴C₅ = ³⁵C₅.
lines: on the pair with the smallest top number:

recall.must_convey: That the identity n C r minus one plus n C r equals n plus one C r is used on ³⁴C₄ + ³⁴C₅ to give ³⁵C₅.
accept: n C r minus one plus n C r is n plus one C r so thirty four C four plus thirty four C five is thirty five C five
use the Pascal identity on the two terms with thirty four on top to get thirty five C five
combine thirty four C four and thirty four C five into thirty five C five
thirty four C four plus thirty four C five ni identity tho thirty five C five ga rayali
the identity turns the pair of thirty fours into thirty five C five

steps.why: The identity ⁿCᵣ₋₁ + ⁿCᵣ = ⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾Cᵣ raises the top number by one while the lower number stays at 5. Each use produces a ³⁵C₅, then ³⁶C₅, and so on — a term of exactly the shape the next pair needs.
common_mistakes: Writing the identity as ⁿCᵣ + ⁿCᵣ = ⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾Cᵣ — the two lower numbers must differ by one.
Starting from ³⁸C₄ instead of the smallest pair; only the pair 34 has a C₅ partner.

steps.label: Repeat until one term remains
steps.margin_note: Two marks. The new ³⁵C₅ joins ³⁵C₄ to make ³⁶C₅, and so on up to ³⁹C₅. Show each line; the examiner is paying for the chain, not the last symbol.

recall.must_convey: That the identity is applied again and again — 35, 36, 37, 38 — and the whole sum collapses to ³⁹C₅.
accept: keep combining thirty five C five with thirty five C four and so on until only thirty nine C five is left
repeat the identity four more times and the answer is thirty nine C five
the sum collapses step by step to thirty nine C five
same identity ni repeat cheste final ga thirty nine C five vasthundi
thirty six C five then thirty seven then thirty eight then thirty nine C five

steps.why: Every application removes one term and raises the top number by one, so five terms of C₄ lift ³⁴C₅ to ³⁹C₅. The sum was built so that it collapses; writing the chain shows the examiner you know why.
common_mistakes: Stopping at ³⁸C₅ — the last term ³⁸C₄ still has to be absorbed.
Changing the lower number to 4 along the way; it stays 5 at every step.
Jumping to ³⁹C₅ with no lines between — the two marks are for the chain.
